version: Player-led experiments v16: chosen purposes, optional strategy help, unrestricted verification and evidence judgments

checks: Every positive allocation is allowed in a third test regardless of earlier balance, except exact repeats
All 20 trios have opt-in goal-specific editable examples and real recorded purposes; no strategy is selected for the player
Goal feedback acknowledges shared attention, unchanged effort and shifted priorities without equating any with learning
Every possible integer split preserves total 100, range 1–98 and deterministic effort
Either remaining card confirms the pair after any first-card choice
Both equal remaining sliders can move in either direction before confirmation
Available bounds clamp safely, reserving one percent, without changing locked weights or snapshots
Near-even accepts gaps through 10 points inclusively, rejects 11, and produces three medium shots
Run requires all three confirmed weights (including the linked pair) and a valid complete allocation
The second experiment requires a changed split and never forces a direction or degree of balance
The reported 43/29/28 → 34/33/33 → 28/43/29 example labels every effort comparison and names its reference test
Comparisons follow each metric identity through reordered runs and distinguish changed weights from unchanged effort
All trio prompts stay single-question and concise while preserving the same optional valid suggestions
Actual trial snapshots and partner/comparison copies remain independent after removing the forecast layer
All 20 trios retain the original animation request fields without generated peer-story data
Every valid integer split uses the 10-point near-even boundary and the correct one/two higher-reward family
All 20 trios have concise pattern-specific reviews; near-even exposes the scoring stopping rule
Second-result questions describe actual increases, decreases and unchanged effort bands
All verification routes and both comparison orders describe the latest actual pattern without assuming an improvement
No dialogue or emoji repeats within 8,640 complete trial paths, including repeated patterns and unchanged scene intensity
Six Level 1 review questions and all 20 Level 2 trio exchanges differ; player names remain supplied text
Player-purpose dialogue and all three scene readings stay fresh across uniform and mixed patterns, every trio and all purpose combinations
No experiment aim or strategy is preselected; keyboard aim choice preserves confirmed weights, and operation guidance remains separate
Strategy help is hidden until requested, follows the selected aim and only loads editable unconfirmed weights; a player can reject the example
Three actual uneven trials can finish; unchanged effort is valid evidence, exact allocation repeats are explained, and every chosen purpose is recorded
The player judges the evidence before the final response; keeping a split produces a matching question and the preview still ends at Goodhart’s Law

At a 720px window height, scrolling to the closing evidence lets three near-even tests finish without inserting a contrasting example; shared attention is acknowledged while stopping at the checklist remains visible
Both judgments are accepted without correctness scores and the comparison fits 1366/768/390/320px
The compact goal choices and collapsed hints fit phone, tablet and desktop without horizontal overflow
No runtime errors in purpose selection, optional hints, unrestricted trials, judgments or the theory endpoint
The task is a prominent 24px question card with a four-pixel accent and three finite pulses; hidden time pauses the animation and the card stays readable after it ends
The player-selected question and optional Apply suggested weights button load editable values, announce the result, stop the attention cue and still require manual confirmation
Reduced motion uses one steady outline, and the 320px task card and explicit suggestion button remain readable and usable
The exact reported three-trial example names every comparison baseline and labels increases, decreases and equal effort even when weights change; ambiguous full-cell highlighting is removed
All three records, comparison bases and change labels fit 1366/768/390/320px without horizontal overflow
No runtime errors in task animation, editable suggestions, three actual trials or responsive comparison
Opening-supplied player name reaches Level 3 labels, avatar and the three weighted partner shots
Level 3 completes once after three player-led tests with immutable tested runs and an explicit near-even/uneven comparison payload
Comparison leads to theory; even duplicate final callbacks stay in the placeholder and never invoke Design Lab
Real Gameplay host carries the opening name and sound preference from Level 2 into the new Level 3 chapter
Level 3 preselects the actual Level 2 trio, permits swapping, and has no player Restart control
Reloading the connected host starts fresh from its configured entry level
Hidden-page publication holds its visible-time sequence and resumes without skipping the three weights
Uniform uneven and uniform near-even histories complete once with all actual trials, explicit player decision and compared=null in the partner contract
Real-time publication and evidence arrive one at a time; Web Audio cues play and Sound off silences later updates
No browser errors in partner, chapter handoff or real-time audio checks
All four latest ZIPs are intact, self-contained and byte-identical to their production builds and manifest
The review ZIP contains separate Level 3 and connected Levels 1–3 HTMLs, identical to their tested latest packages
Packaged Level2.html completes 3 → 6 → 10 → 25 → 100 offline with normal motion
Packaged standalone Level3.html completes three player-led tests and compares all actual results offline
Packaged Level1.html includes the latest behaviour and two replies, stops after Level 1 and permits replay
Standalone Level 1 reload starts a fresh Level 1 run
Packaged combined game continues from the current Level 1 into playable Level 2 and keeps sound preference
Packaged combined game connects Level 1 → Level 2 → playable Level 3 in one open run
Combined preview reload starts from Level 1 rather than restoring Level 2
Packaged entries have no browser runtime errors

notes: The prior latest version is frozen on archive/pre-player-experiments-v15 at d3075b72950e8bf9a0f693d15cf37b95440cfe7d, with its existing downloads. Existing archives and versioned ZIPs are preserved.

Each editor asks the player to select attention, priority or exploration without a default or correctness score. Radio choices support keyboard input and preserve slider values and confirmations. The selected purpose is recorded in the actual WeightRun.

The operational guide remains separate. Strategy hints are collapsed under Need a hint? and adapt to the chosen purpose. Applying an example explicitly loads editable, unconfirmed values and never runs it. The browser rejects the optional example and completes its own trials.

Any distinct positive integer allocation totaling 100 can be the third test, irrespective of weight-pattern class or unchanged effort bands. All valid integer splits are checked against representative uniform and mixed histories; zero and exact repeats remain rejected. Both three uneven and three near-even player histories complete without system references.

A short finding and the teacher question address the chosen purpose. Shared attention can be acknowledged without treating it as evidence of deeper learning. Near-even still exposes criteria, ticks and stopping. Three near-even readings have three distinct replies per metric; third-test dialogue no longer assumes a priority switch occurred.

The comparison shows all actual trial purposes and retains named previous-test effort comparisons. The player chooses keep or rethink before Watch Alex’s response. Both choices are accepted, affect the response opening and carry through the partner/completion contracts. Completion fires once after the explicit judgment. compared remains the copied near-even/uneven pair for mixed histories and is null for uniform histories; documentation and host tests cover this deliberate contract change.

Current dialogue validation includes the preceding 8,640 cross-level scenario paths and 3,240 purpose/history/trio paths, with both final judgments checked against earlier chapter lines and emojis. Representative all-near-even, all-uneven, same-band and mixed histories do not repeat lines or emoji. Replay remains deterministic.

The final production browser checks 1366/768/390/320px layouts, finite/hidden/reduced-motion task cues, editable hints, both judgments and the exact prior effort-comparison example. The 720px-height test scrolls to the closing evidence, allowing its visible-time sequence to finish; package-flow tests likewise scroll to the information being read rather than advancing hidden content.

Partner tests verify opening names, the editable inherited Level 2 trio, copied actual trials and purposes, judgment routing, nullable compared pairs, once-only completion, real-time report/evidence cues and hidden-page pauses. Custom renderers replace the whole placeholder, including for uniform histories. The final endpoint remains theory.reveal; no Design Lab callback is invoked.

All four final builds and all five latest ZIPs pass. CRC, source, build, HTML and ZIP hashes are checked, and actual packaged standalone Levels 1/2/3 plus the connected game complete their relevant offline routes. The review bundle contains standalone Level 3 and connected Levels 1–3 from those same builds.

Opening integration and finished authored animation scripts are outside this change. These checks establish functional behaviour, not measured learning effectiveness, user-browser local-file opening or classroom hosting capacity.
